literal_statement: There exists w in C_0^infty([0,1]) with int_0^1 w = 1 and a universal constant C_3>0 such that for all iid centered X with EX^2=1, EX^3=0, E|X|^5<inf, sup_x |P(sum_{n=1}^{N-1} sqrt(w(n/N)/A_N) X_n <= x) - G(x)| <= C_3 E|X|^5 N^{-3/2}, where A_N = sum_{n=0}^{N-1} w(n/N) and G(x) = Phi(x) - (E|X|^4-3)/(8 sqrt(2pi) N) (x^3-3x) e^{-x^2/2}.

mechanism: Weighted Edgeworth expansion: the N^{-1} correction coefficient for the weighted standardized sum is (EX^4-3) * (sum_i w(n_i/N)^2)/A_N^2 -> (EX^4-3) int w^2 /(int w)^2 (1/N). By Cauchy-Schwarz int w^2 >= (int w)^2 with equality iff w is constant a.e., impossible for compactly supported w; hence the coefficient 1 in G(x) is unattainable for any admissible w.
